hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $-1$.
And the point at $-1$ is *not* filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything strictly **greater than $-1$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 1. A line running to the right starts at negative 1 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/aed0263f93da423bc6baf8f541edfd70a0c6fe9e)

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < -1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 1. A line running to the left starts at negative 1 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/3a126afb3e7bf25f070092eae621d17f0e4df03d)

The graph of $x \leq -1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A solid point is plotted at negative 1. A line running to the left starts at negative 1 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/175f0c9151882553a4be9ed80682e7f1538f7ef1)

The graph of $x \geq -1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A solid point is plotted at negative 1. A line running to the right starts at negative 1 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/490e0d6489782fef935b8e7936484fb7ca874a7f)
